title: Robe Pork
paragraphs: It was the evening of the week after I’d started living at the Colosseum. Father decided to take Big Sisters to the port of Zeltoble. Naturally, I tagged along too.

After all, Zeltoble is a place of both Light and Darkness. This is the port on the side of Darkness, and it has quite a gloomy atmosphere. Then, as if to fulfill a promise, Father called out to a monster merchant.
“Well, well, the Shield—no, Lord Lokk. Hello.”

The monster merchant of Zeltoble greeted Father with a smile. Huh? Is that Father’s alias? I remember he named the territory he pioneered in the first world after that. Well, knowing Father, he probably just tweaked his last name to come up with it. I think it’s a pretty fitting alias.
“I heard the slaves I ordered have arrived?”
“Yes, they’re right here… Well, thanks to the assistance from the Haven Trading Company, the local merchants said it was much easier to procure them, which was a great help.”
“I see…”

The monster merchant is busily having carriages unloaded from the ship and giving orders. The figure in a full-length robe following alongside the carriage is quite striking. It seems Father, acting as the representative, is introducing the person wearing that robe—someone arranged by the monster merchant.
“Raphtalia, Sadeena, please check the cargo.”
“Y-yes.”
“Okay!”

By the way, Filo-chan and the other Filolials are waiting in the rear. They don’t particularly care for the gloomy atmosphere of Zeltoble’s Dark Harbor, but since they know the carriage will be unloaded soon, they’re waiting with bated breath. The older sisters are peering inside the carriage to check on things. I took a quick peek inside as well—there was a cage set up inside, and some familiar Demi-Humans were huddled together in one spot with somber expressions. Right then, the Older Sister appeared in the form everyone knows her by: her Therianthrope form.
“Hellooo. Is everyone okay?”
“Buh?”
“Ah, Sadeena-san…”
“Buh-buh!”

Oh, now that they’ve seen a familiar face, everyone is rushing over to my Older Sister’s Older Sister all at once. As expected of Older Sister, she’s incredibly trustworthy. Since she was trusted by Filo-chan and Lord Filolial in the first world as well, this is only to be expected.
“Big Sisters and I are going to take you all to a safe place right now, so you can rest easy.”
“Buh… Buh?”
Older Sister is smiling cheerfully. She’s so good with kids—her handling of them rivals even Father’s.
“So, I’m going to tell you something that might surprise you all. Even I was surprised when I first saw her. Believe it or not, the child here is actually Raphtalia-chan.”
“Y-yes. “It’s been a while, everyone.”
“B, B-B-B-B-B!?”

Oh? A pig that looks just like Keel is staring intently at my Older Sister from inside its cage. But… could the difference in how quickly they came to believe her be related to the level of trust that had already been established before this happened? It took a little while to get Big Sister and her friends to believe me. But just having Big Sister’s Older Sister here has allowed me to gain their trust this quickly… Big Sister’s Older Sister must be quite trusted, huh.
“Alright, everyone, after you count to make sure there aren’t any unfamiliar kids here, line up so we can check easily.”
“Okay!”
“Boo-boo!”
With all that, it seems the headcount wrapped up fairly quickly. Big Sister calls out to Father.
“Okay. I’ve confirmed everyone from the village is here. It looks like some kids aren’t feeling well, but we should be able to manage.”
“I see… So.”

Father shifts his gaze toward a figure in a loose-fitting robe. I believe this is the fellow who helped with the villagers’ gathering, or something like that. He looks suspicious at first glance. But the Haven Trading Company… I feel like I’ve heard that name somewhere before. Where was it, though?　Was it in the first world? No, that was…
“I appreciate your help… but what’s your motive? Money?”
“…Boo, bu-bu-bu-bu-hee.”
The figure in the robe let out a somewhat listless sound. That sound… I feel like I’ve heard it somewhere before.
“…And what’s the point of that?”
Hmm… I don’t understand Pig-speak. It’d be easier if he’d just become a talking dog like Keel… Actually, even a talking pig-therianthrope from Siltvelt would be fine.
“Miss, what did he say?”
“He’s saying that in exchange for a discount on the price, he wants to have a say in Lord Naofumi’s actions… Is that right? You’re the Hero, so why don’t you understand what he’s saying?”
“Because he’s a pig, that’s why.”
“Huh?”
I can tell at a glance that Father is growing increasingly wary of this behavior, which seems to have no clear purpose. Then the pig in the robe raised one hand and began grunting repeatedly.
“Oink, oink… oink, oink-oink-oink, oink-oink-oink.”
After that, Father suddenly looked at me for some reason before asking the pig in the robe again. It’s driving me crazy. As I twirled my spear to suppress my frustration, my Older Sister explained:

“...Honestly, I hate not knowing when he’ll come to kill me to silence me. Since that’s the case, I figure I’d have a better chance of surviving if I bring some kind of gift to negotiate with, so that’s why I’m cooperating like this. “Don’t you get it?” she says.”

That’s when I realized exactly who this guy was. A summer insect flying into the Fire. If he came here of his own accord, I’ll stab him to death. Die in disgrace, cursing the world! That’s what I’ll do.
“B, b-b-b-b-b? B-b-b-b-b.”
Without a moment’s hesitation, Father reached out his hand, as if to stop me.

“I haven’t told anyone about Motoyasu’s atrocities, and my business instincts are telling me the winds are in our favor… but I never imagined I’d run into you here—you who managed to escape from Motoyasu.”
“B-b-b-b-b”

Stopped by Father, I had no choice but to stop aiming my spear at the robe-wearing pig… I mean, Elena, the Lazy Pig. If I were alone, I’d have killed her, but since Father stopped me, there’s nothing I can do. After all, this one was actually useful in a previous loop. Depending on the situation, she might still be of some use. If she’s worthless, I’ll just have to dispose of her.
“So? Is it true you haven’t heard any rumors about Motoyasu’s atrocities?”
“Bub.”

“That is certainly true. Yes. I cannot say exactly what information you’re referring to, but within the scope of what we’ve been able to gather, we haven’t heard of any commotion involving the real Shield Hero and Spear Hero within Melromarc. Yes.”

Hmm, as always, the Lazy Pig is out to save his own skin. Well, if word had spread, we’d eventually have to go and kill them. But since they mentioned “the real ones,” it seems there’s a fake Father out there. Fakes appeared frequently in the previous loop as well, so it’s not particularly unusual. Still, it’s impressive how these guys can tell the difference between the real and the fake. Soon, Father—who had been following up on the matter—confronts the monster merchant in Zeltoble, glaring at him while jingling his money pouch and demanding an answer.
“Is that true? If it’s a lie, my mad dogs will turn this port into a sea of Fire.”

Oh… that’s Father’s specialty: intimidation. By the way, who exactly is this “mad dog”? My Older Sister, perhaps? No, I’m sure he’s talking about Keel. But I don’t think Keel is that strong these days, you know?

I remember how he flew into a rage and attacked me just for picking a crepe from the crepe tree. Ever since then, he’s gotten angry and attacked me every time I’ve taken even a single crepe. Well, after a while, I got pretty good at dodging him, though. HAHAHA.
“That’s correct. Yes. All we’ve heard is that plants are multiplying in the village to the southwest.”
“Hmm… That doesn’t seem to have anything to do with it.”
After tossing the money pouch to the monster merchant, Father turns his gaze toward the Lazy Pig. Plants, you say?
“So, what’s your goal here?”
“Oink, oink-oink-oink. Oink-oink.”
As usual, I have absolutely no idea what the Lazy Pig is saying. But if I leave it to Father, everything will work out fine.
“That person gave us a proper meal on the ship.”
The boy—one of Big Sister’s friends—is backing him up.
“So you’re trying to curry favor with us just when it suits you… What a hassle…”
Since I have no idea what they’re talking about, I’m looking around in confusion when Father turns back with a sigh.

“Ask him what his goal is. I’ll keep quiet about what you did. He brought the village slaves as a gift, so he’s proposing that we guarantee their lives and let them work under our command until this whole thing blows over.”
Oh… I see.
“That’s some Lazy Pig logic, isn’t it?”

His survival instinct is unnecessarily strong, and he’s calculating with a decent grasp of the situation. Come to think of it, he’s survived through many loops. Since he was alive in the first world too, his tenacity must be quite something.
“So, Motoyasu. Can we trust this guy?”
“Well… at the very least, he was still alive even after peace was restored. I recall him being one of Father’s business partners.”
“Huh?”
“So, there are some issues, but he’s not exactly an enemy, then?”
“By the way, aside from the first world, there was a time when he worked under Father and helped with the business. It’s frustrating to admit, but he seems to be quite good at business.”
I can’t lie to Father, after all. Even if he is a Lazy Pig, let’s make sure to properly inform him of his specs and track record.
“I see… Well then, if you become a slave who obeys me absolutely, I’ll make sure not to set Motoyasu on you to silence you. Is that okay?”
“Oink.”
The Lazy Pig nodded.
“Is that really okay, Lord Naofumi?”
“As long as the slave mark works properly, there shouldn’t be a problem. If he tries to spill any confidential information—including that incident—I’ll just have him dealt with.”
Father is explaining the situation to my worried Older Sister. He’s absolutely right. Well, I can’t imagine this Lazy Pig would do anything to put himself at a disadvantage.
“Oh my… What on earth are you talking about?”
“Um… Sadeena, I’ll explain that later. Lord Naofumi is hardly at fault here—it’s a problem caused by the Spear Hero.”
“Oh my—”
“Anyway, are these all the people from Raphtalia’s village?”
“No…”
“Well, we’ll keep looking for more… but for now, let’s get these guys loaded up. Filo and the others—!”
“‘‘‘Yes, sir!’’”
Led by Filo-chan, the Filolials start pulling the carriage as if they’ve been waiting for this moment. Amidst all this, I call out to Luna-chan.
“Luna-chan, that’s probably Keel. If you raise him and have your Older Sister teach him how to turn back into a dog, I think you’ll have a lot of fun, Luna-chan.”
“Yeah. Got it.”
Luna-chan still doesn’t talk much, but she seems to have understood what I said. And so, after gathering the village slaves, Father and the others were escorted to our temporary home in Zeltoble.

After that, Big Sister and her Older Sister announced their plan to the villagers: to prevent any more people like themselves from being produced, everyone must become stronger together; and eventually, as practice for rebuilding the village, they set a goal to engage in trade with Lady Filolial and the others under Father’s leadership. I was there too, but since it was a familiar scene, I’ll skip the details. To be honest, I was too distracted by Luna-chan staring intently at Keel, who was showing his enthusiasm by chirping at everyone.
“It’s so lively—Filo, this is fun!”
Filo-tan was having a great time, getting caught up in the excitement. I had a blast, too!
My joy is my joy. Filo-tan’s joy is also my joy! Together, it’s happiness. Everything is shared.
“Well… we’re becoming quite a large group, and I’m starting to feel a bit fed up…”
“First, we’ll tempt everyone with Father’s cooking!”
“You said that as if it were the most natural thing in the world.”
After all, Father has always treated us to a meal. Even the Filolials are all drooling at the thought of getting to eat his cooking.
“Master’s dinner—”
Even Filo is joining in.
“You lot have bottomless appetites, so you’ll have to wait.”
“That’s too harsh, Father!”
“Shut up. Ah, I wish rice would just sprout from the ground…”
Hm? I have a feeling I’m forgetting something. Oh, that’s right—I forgot to retrieve the Bio-Plant.
“I have an idea where it might be.”
“Hm? Is that so?”
“It is.”
“Well, if you say so, I suppose it must be there…”
Would you believe it? Father seems uneasy about what I just said. I’m a useful guy, you know. To prove it, I absolutely must go retrieve those Bio-Plant seeds.
“There won’t be any problems, right? Can’t we handle this peacefully without any unnecessary deaths?”
“Of course. Well then, I’ll be off for a quick run. Lady Filolial!　If you’re hungry, come along!”
“Ah, uh…”
That Lazy Pig was watching the whole thing, but I’m ignoring him. That Lazy Pig has absolutely no influence on this world. In fact, he should just stay lying down until the moment he dies.
“Filo’s not going.”
“Neither is Luna.”
“Kou’s going!”
So Filo-tan and Luna-chan will be staying home. I wonder if this will lighten Father’s load a bit today?
“Well then, since I’m out here anyway, maybe I’ll go fishing. Naofumi-chan, I’m counting on you to take care of everyone’s meals.”
“Yeah, yeah… Thank goodness we’re in the Land of Zeltoble, where no one sleeps. I guess I’ll head to the market and buy some ingredients we can eat.”
“Filo’s gonna help!”
Hmm, hmm… A meal made from the ingredients brought back by Father and Filo-tan… I’m already looking forward to it so much. I’d better hurry up and take down that Bio-Plant to retrieve the seeds.
“Well then, I’ll go clean up Keel-kun and the others.”
“Luna’s gonna help, too!”
Oh, they’re working together so well. Everyone’s bursting with enthusiasm. I can’t let them outdo me.
